questions.question: A vendor packed 96 eggs into three boxes: X, Y and Z. There are twice as many eggs in the Z box as there are in the X box, and twice as many in the X and Y boxes combined as there are in the Z box. How many eggs did he pack in the Y box?
questions.solution:
According to question:

X + Y + Z = 96 -------(1)

and, Z = 2X ----------(2)

and, X + Y = 2Z --------(3)

Put value of Z in equation (1) and (3)

X + Y + Z = 96

2Z + Z = 96

3Z = 96

Z = 32

Put the value of Z in equation (2)

Z = 2X

2X = 32

X = 16

Put the value of X and Z in Equation 1

X + Y + Z = 96 

16 + Y + 32 = 96

Y + 48 = 96

Y = 48

Hence, **"48" **is the correct answer.

questions.question: A person appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, before entering upon his Office, has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before

options.text: President, or some person appointed by him

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President or some person appointed by him**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Oath or Affirmation**

__
 
• A person appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, before entering upon his office, has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before **the President, or some person appointed by him for this purpose**. **Hence, option 2 is correct.**
 
• **In his oath, a judge of the Supreme Court swears:**
 
 
• to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India;
 
• to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India;
 
• to duly and faithfully and to the best of his ability, knowledge and judgement perform the duties of the Office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will; and
 
• to uphold the Constitution and the laws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Qualifications of Judges**

 
• A person to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court should have the following qualifications:
 
 
• He should be a citizen of India.
 
• He should have been a judge of a High Court (or high courts in succession) for five years; or
 
• He should have been an advocate of a High Court (or High Courts in succession) for ten years; or
 
• He should be a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the president.
 
 

**From the above, it is clear that the Constitution has not prescribed minimum age for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.**

• In the Iqta system, the lands of the Delhi Sultanate were divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned these Iqtas to Sultan's soldiers, officers, and nobles.
 
• Major changes were seen in this during the reign of **Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316)**.
 
• Unlimited **expansion of the boundaries** of the empire and **imposition of full rent on the peasantry** settled in the old areas – both these works were done simultaneously.
 
• Along with this **unprecedented increase in the revenue** of the ruling class, many such steps were taken which affected the Iqta system.
 
• Now the entire **Central Doab and some parts of modern Kolkhand** came under the Khalisa.
 
• The practice of naming villages as pay Iqtas to Sultan's personal cavalry was abolished.
 
• The **entire revenue** of the Khalisa was deposited in the **treasury** and the salaries of the soldiers were paid in cash.
 
•

questions.question:
Arrange the following social movements in chronological order of their emergence:

I. Tebhaga Movement

II. Self-Respect Movement

III. Khilafat Movement

IV. Telangana Peasant Uprising
questions.solution:
**Answer: The correct answer is, c) **III, II, IV, I

**Solution

The Self-Respect Movement**, initiated by E.V. Ramasamy Naicker in 1925, aimed to abolish discrimination against non-Brahmins and promote rational and humanistic thought in Tamil Nadu.

**The Khilafat Movement**, launched in 1919, was a pan-Islamic movement that sought to protest the harsh terms imposed on the Ottoman Empire by the Allied Powers after World War I.

**The Tebhaga Movement** erupted in 1946-1947 in Bengal, where peasants demanded a two-thirds share of their harvest against the existing practice of giving half to the landlords.

**The Telangana Peasant Uprising**, also known as the Telangana Rebellion, was a peasant revolt that took place in the Telangana region of Hyderabad State from 1946 to 1951, against the feudal system of forced labor and oppressive taxation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

 

**Self-Respect Movement**

__
 
• Emerged in 1925 in Tamil Nadu, led by E.V. Ramasamy Naicker (also known as Periyar)
 
• Aimed to eradicate the caste system and promote equality and rationalism
 
• Advocated for the rights and emancipation of non-Brahmin communities
 
• Challenged Brahminical dominance and sought to reform Hinduism
 
• Promoted self-respect and social justice for marginalized groups
 
• Criticized superstitions, religious rituals, and Hindu revivalism
 
• Advocated for women's rights, including the right to property and education
 
• Encouraged inter-caste marriages and the use of the Tamil language
 
• Established the Self-Respect Movement as a political and social force in Tamil Nadu

 

**Khilafat Movement**

 
• Pan-Islamic movement launched in 1919 to protest the harsh treatment of the Ottoman Empire after World War I
 
• Supported by Indian Muslims and led by prominent leaders like Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Abul Kalam Azad, and the Ali Brothers
 
• Aimed to preserve the authority of the Ottoman Sultan as the Caliph (spiritual leader) of the Muslim world
 
• Gained momentum after the Treaty of Sèvres, which dismembered the Ottoman Empire and threatened the status of the Caliph
 
• Mobilized Muslims across India to participate in non-violent civil disobedience and boycotts against British rule
 
• Forged an alliance with the Indian National Congress and Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement
 
• Led to the Hijrat Movement, where some Muslims migrated to Afghanistan in protest
 
• Faded after the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924
 
• Contributed to the growth of Muslim nationalism and the demand for a separate Muslim state

 

**Tebhaga Movement**

 
• Peasant uprising in Bengal in 1946-1947, led by the Krishak Praja Party and the Communist Party of India
 
• Demanded a two-thirds share of the harvest for peasants, instead of the existing practice of giving half to the landlords
 
• Protested against the oppressive zamindari system and exploitative practices of landlords
 
• Gained support from sharecroppers, bargadars (peasants who received a share of the crop), and agricultural laborers
 
• Faced brutal repression from the colonial authorities and zamindars, leading to violence and loss of life
 
• Highlighted the need for land reforms and the abolition of the zamindari system
 
• Contributed to the growth of the communist movement and the rise of peasant activism in Bengal
 
• Influenced the subsequent Bargadari Acts, which granted greater rights to bargadars

 

**Telangana Peasant Uprising**

 
• Peasant revolt in the Telangana region of Hyderabad State from 1946 to 1951
 
• Protested against the feudal system of forced labor (vetti) and oppressive taxation by landlords and the Nizam's government
 
• Led by the Communist Party of India and supported by peasants, agricultural laborers, and the Andhra Mahasabha
 
• Adopted guerrilla tactics, including attacking landlords, occupying villages, and establishing parallel administrations
 
• Faced brutal suppression by the Nizam's forces, known as the "Razakars," leading to widespread violence
 
• Highlighted the need for land reforms and the abolition of the feudal system
 
• Contributed to the growth of the communist movement and peasant activism in the region
 
• Influenced the subsequent land reforms and abolition of the zamindari system in Telangana after its integration with India

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**These social movements played a crucial role in shaping the political and social landscape of India during the colonial and post-independence eras. They challenged existing power structures, advocated for the rights of marginalized communities, and sought to address long-standing grievances related to social, economic, and religious issues.

The Self-Respect Movement, led by Periyar E.V. Ramasamy Naicker, had a profound impact on Tamil society. It empowered non-Brahmin communities, challenged the caste system, and promoted rationalism and social justice. The movement's emphasis on self-respect and equality resonated with many and paved the way for subsequent Dravidian movements in Tamil Nadu.

The Khilafat Movement, although short-lived, played a significant role in galvanizing Muslim support for the Indian independence movement. Its alliance with the Indian National Congress and Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement highlighted the potential for Hindu-Muslim unity against British rule. However, the eventual abolition of the Caliphate and the failure to protect Muslim interests contributed to the growth of Muslim nationalism and the demand for a separate Muslim state.

The Tebhaga Movement and the Telangana Peasant Uprising were rooted in the struggle against oppressive land revenue systems and the exploitation of peasants by landlords. These movements not only demanded a fair share of the harvest and the abolition of forced labor but also challenged the existing power structures and highlighted the need for land reforms. Their impact resonated long after independence, influencing subsequent legislation and policies related to land ownership and tenant rights.

These social movements demonstrated the power of collective action and grassroots mobilization in challenging established systems of oppression and inequality. They served as catalysts for broader social and political changes, paving the way for the emancipation of marginalized groups and the transformation of Indian society in the post-independence era.

questions.question:
Consider the statements about the Ryotwari system:

Statement A: The Ryotwari system created a direct relationship with the individual farmers for revenue collection.

Statement B: The Ryotwari system primarily utilized the village headman to collect revenue.

options.text: Statement A is true, but Statement B is false.
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true.
Both Statement A and Statement B are true.
Both Statement A and Statement B are false.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - Statement A is true, but Statement B is false.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A: The Ryotwari system created a direct relationship with the individual farmers for revenue collection.**

 
 
• The Ryotwari system was introduced by the British East India Company in parts of India such as Madras (now Tamil Nadu) and Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• Under this system, the government dealt directly with the peasant (or ryot) for the collection of land revenue.
 
• Each farmer was responsible for paying taxes directly to the government based on the land they owned or cultivated.
 
• This system aimed to eliminate the role of intermediaries, thereby providing a direct link between the government and the individual farmers.
 
 
 
• **Statement B: The Ryotwari system primarily utilized the village headman to collect revenue.**
 
 
• In contrast, the Ryotwari system did not primarily rely on the village headman for revenue collection.
 
• The government's direct interaction with individual farmers was a key characteristic of the Ryotwari system.
 
• Revenue was assessed on the cultivable land each farmer held, and farmers paid taxes directly to the government, bypassing any village intermediaries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ryotwari System**

 
 
• Introduced in the early 19th century by Thomas Munro and Captain Alexander Read.
 
• It was different from the Zamindari system, which involved landlords or zamindars as intermediaries.
 
• Focused on making the peasant the direct owner of the land, responsible for paying taxes and maintaining land records.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari System**
 
 
• The Zamindari system involved revenue collection through landlords or zamindars who collected taxes from peasants on behalf of the government.
 
• The Zamindars played a vital role as intermediaries between the government and the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari System**
 
 
• Another land revenue system introduced by the British, which involved revenue collection at the village level, often through the village headman or chiefs.
 
• Revenue was assessed collectively on a village or mahal (an administrative unit).

questions.question: ______ is a food component that provides energy, while __________ helps in building and repairing body cells.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Carbohydrates, Proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbohydrates** are the primary source of energy for the body. They are broken down into glucose, which is used by the body to produce energy for various activities.
 
• They are found in foods such as **rice, bread, pasta, potatoes, fruits, and vegetables**.
 
• **Proteins**, on the other hand, are responsible for the growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues. They are essential for the formation of enzymes, hormones, and other body chemicals.
 
• Proteins are found in foods like **meat, fish, eggs, dairy products, beans, and legumes**.
 
• The combination of carbohydrates and proteins ensures that the body is supplied with energy and has the necessary components for cellular repair and growth.
 
• Both **macronutrients** play critical roles in maintaining overall health and well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fats, Carbohydrates**__

 __
 
• **Fats** are a dense source of energy and provide essential fatty acids that the body cannot produce on its own. However, they are not primarily involved in building or repairing body cells.
 
• Carbohydrates, as explained earlier, are the main energy providers for the body.
 
 
 
• **Proteins, Fats**__
 __
 
• While **proteins** are essential for building and repairing body cells, **fats** primarily serve as a secondary energy source and are not involved in cellular repair or growth to the same extent as proteins.
 
 
 
• **Fats, Vitamins**__
 
 
• Fats provide energy and help in the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins like **A, D, E, and K**, but they are not a primary energy source like carbohydrates.
 
• **Vitamins** do not provide energy but are essential for various metabolic processes and maintaining good health.

questions.question:
Assertion: Physical changes can be reversed, but chemical changes cannot.

Reason: In a physical change, no new substances are formed, and the original material can often be restored.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct, but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect, but Reason is correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Physical changes** can often be reversed because they do not alter the chemical structure of a substance (e.g., melting ice).
 
• **Chemical changes** result in the formation of new substances with different chemical properties, making them generally irreversible (e.g., burning paper).
 
• In a **physical change**, the substance retains its original identity, as no new substances are formed.
 
• The reason provided correctly explains the assertion, as the reversibility of physical changes is tied to the fact that no new chemical bonds are formed or broken.
 
• The concept aligns with fundamental principles of chemistry, distinguishing physical and chemical changes based on molecular transformations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Changes:**

 
 
• Examples include melting, boiling, freezing, condensation, and dissolving.
 
• Physical changes are often reversible as no chemical composition is altered.
 
• They involve changes in state, shape, or size.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Changes:**
 
 
• Examples include rusting of iron, digestion of food, and combustion of wood.
 
• Chemical changes involve breaking and forming new chemical bonds, resulting in new substances.
 
• These changes are generally irreversible under normal conditions.
 
 
 
• **Indicators of Chemical Changes:**
 
 
• Color change, gas production, temperature change, and formation of precipitate are key indicators.
 
• Energy is often absorbed or released in the form of heat, light, or sound.
 
 
 
• **Reversibility in Physical vs. Chemical Changes:**
 
 
• While most physical changes are reversible, some, like breaking glass, may be irreversible practically.
 
• Chemical changes are usually irreversible because they involve new substances with different molecular structures.

questions.question: The L.C.M. of two prime numbers, x and y (x > y) is 161. Then the value of (x - y) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The L.C.M. of two distinct prime numbers is exactly equal to their product.

Product of primes x and y = 161.

By finding prime factors, 161 = 23 × 7.

Since x > y, we directly assign x = 23 and y = 7.

Therefore, x − y = 23 − 7 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two prime numbers x and y = 161

x > y

**Concept Used:**

For any two distinct prime numbers, their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is equal to their product, as they do not share any common factors other than 1.

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(x, y) = x × y = 161

⇒ Prime factorization of 161 = 7 × 23

⇒ Since x and y are prime numbers and x > y:

⇒ x = 23

⇒ y = 7

⇒ We need to find the value of (x − y):

⇒ x − y = 23 − 7

⇒ x − y = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two or more prime numbers is always equal to their product, since they have no common factors other than 1.

HCF of Prime Numbers

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of any two distinct prime numbers is always 1.

Co-Prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. All pairs of distinct prime numbers are co-prime by definition, but composite numbers can also form co-prime pairs (e.g., 8 and 15).

Parallelogram Law of Diagonals

In any parallelogram, the sum of the squares of the lengths of the diagonals is always strictly equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the four sides: d₁² + d₂² = 2(a² + b²).

Since diagonals bisect each other forming equivalent sub-triangles with the main sides, the parallelogram diagonal property acts as a direct scaling application of Apollonius's Theorem: AB² + BC² = 2 × (BM² + AM²), where M is the intersection point of both diagonals.

Area of a Parallelogram

The total area can be uniquely calculated either by using the base and perpendicular height rule (Area = base × height) or geometrically using adjacent sides and the included angle (Area = a × b × sin θ).
</p

questions.question: In a 100-m race, A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 5 m. In the same race, A beats C by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of distances A : B = 100 : (100 − 20) = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

Ratio of distances B : C = 100 : (100 − 5) = 100 : 95 = 20 : 19

Combining the ratios by making B equal ⇒ A : B : C = (5 × 5) : (4 × 5) : 19 = 25 : 20 : 19

For a 100 m race, multiply the combined ratio by 4 ⇒ A : B : C = 100 : 80 : 76

When A finishes 100 m, C runs 76 m. Gap = 100 − 76 = 24 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance of the race = 100 m

A beats B by 20 m ⇒ When A runs 100 m, B runs 80 m.

B beats C by 5 m ⇒ When B runs 100 m, C runs 95 m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f7ae2cc3d4c5e9f0bdd5355ea234baa0fd5218927fcad3f8be690316fa3af18.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For the same time duration, Distance is directly proportional to Speed.

Ratio of distances covered = Ratio of speeds

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance ratio of A and B = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

⇒ Distance ratio of B and C = 100 : 95 = 20 : 19

⇒ To find the distance covered by C when A completes 100 m, we can relate C's distance to A's by using B's distance.

⇒ When B covers 100 m, C covers 95 m.

⇒ When B covers 1 m, C covers 95 ÷ 100 = 0.95 m.

⇒ When B covers 80 m (the exact moment when A covers 100 m), C covers = 80 × 0.95 = 76 m.

⇒ Distance A beats C by = Total race distance − C's distance covered = 100 − 76 = 24 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Races

If A beats B by x meters in an L-meter race, it directly implies that when A has completed exactly L meters, B has only completed (L − x) meters.

Head Start (Distance)

If A gives B a head start of x meters, A runs the full distance L while B runs only (L − x) meters within the same time span.

Head Start (Time)

If A gives B a head start of t seconds, it implies B starts running t seconds earlier than A, ensuring both finish the race at the same time.

Dead Heat

A situation in a race where two or more participants reach the finish line at the exact same instant.
</p

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 3,00,000, compounded half-yearly, for 2(1)/(2) years at the rate of 20% per annum.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Half-yearly rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% (1/10) and Time = 2.5 × 2 = 5 cycles.

For 5 cycles, P = 10⁵ = 100000 units, A = 11⁵ = 161051 units.

Compound Interest (CI) = 161051 − 100000 = 61051 units.

Since P = 100000 units = Rs. 3,00,000, Total CI = 61051 × 3 = Rs. 1,83,153.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Principal (P) = Rs. 3,00,000

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = 20% per annum

⇒ Time (T) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

⇒ A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dfdcefdfa1e4503188153d36cb3e3121ce34446832030451b92d811ce875048.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since interest is compounded half-yearly, Rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10%

⇒ Number of conversion periods (n) = 2.5 × 2 = 5

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (1 + 10/100)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (11/10)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (161051 / 100000)

⇒ A = 3 × 161051 = 4,83,153

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 4,83,153 − 3,00,000 = 1,83,153

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Additional Information__**

Half-yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the given annual rate is divided by 2, and the total time period in years is multiplied by 2.

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the given annual rate is divided by 4, and the time period is multiplied by 4.

Successive Multiplication Factor

Amount can be directly calculated using successive multiplying factors based on rate fractions. For a 10% rate, the multiplying factor is 11/10 per cycle.
</p

questions.question: Find the mean proportional of 6 and 54.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional of two numbers a and b is directly given by √(a × b).

Given numbers are 6 and 54.

Mean proportional = √(6 × 54)

Mean proportional = √324 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two numbers: 6 and 54

**Formula Used:**

If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a : x :: x : b, which implies x² = a × b.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/75fd9c5c888d6eacea248868983d8663d48f0c2102a78d3569faab6f12fab667.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the mean proportional be x.

⇒ 6 / x = x / 54

⇒ x² = 6 × 54

⇒ x² = 324

⇒ x = √324

⇒ x = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If c is the third proportional to a and b, then a : b :: b : c ⇒ c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If d is the fourth proportional to a, b and c, then a : b :: c : d ⇒ d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given as a² : b².
</p

questions.question: The lengths of one side and a diagonal of a rectangle are 63 cm and 65 cm, respectively. What is the perimeter (in cm) of a square whose area is one-seventh of that of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Pythagorean triplet (16, 63, 65), the width of the rectangle is 16 cm.

Area of the square = (Area of rectangle) ÷ 7 = (63 × 16) ÷ 7

Area of the square = 9 × 16 = 144 cm².

Side of the square = √144 = 12 cm.

Perimeter of the square = 4 × 12 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of one side of the rectangle (l) = 63 cm

Length of the diagonal (d) = 65 cm

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras theorem: d² = l² + w²

Area of rectangle = l × w

Area of square = a²

Perimeter of square = 4 × a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34aa3b9d3a8e03d6254dbc530e625348d0a963cf8c6a1d225b18f5f80da4a980.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ w = √(65² − 63²)

⇒ w = √[(65 − 63) × (65 + 63)]

⇒ w = √(2 × 128) = √256 = 16 cm

⇒ Area of the rectangle = 63 × 16 = 1008 cm²

⇒ Area of the square = 1008 ÷ 7 = 144 cm²

⇒ Side of the square (a) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × 12 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem & Triplets

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides (a² + b² = c²). Common triplets like (16, 63, 65) or (5, 12, 13) frequently appear in exams and greatly save computation time if memorised.

Rectangle Properties

A rectangle has opposite sides equal and parallel. The area is Length × Width. The perimeter is 2 × (Length + Width). The length of the diagonal is √(Length² + Width²).

Square Properties

A square is a special rectangle with all four sides equal. The area is Side². The perimeter is 4 × Side. The length of its diagonal is Side × √2.
</p

questions.question: A person travels equal distances at speeds of 3 km/h, 4 km/h, 7 km/h and 12km/h, and takes a total of 680 minutes. What is the total distance (in km) travelled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let each equal distance segment be the LCM of speeds (3, 4, 7, 12) = 84 km.

Assumed total time for 4 × 84 km = (84/3) + (84/4) + (84/7) + (84/12) = 28 + 21 + 12 + 7 = 68 hours.

Actual total time given = 680 minutes = 680 ÷ 60 = 68/6 hours.

Distance multiplier = Actual Time ÷ Assumed Time = (68/6) ÷ 68 = 1/6.

Total distance = Assumed Total Distance × Multiplier = (4 × 84) × (1/6) = 336 ÷ 6 = 56 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4fff1348c437aaf1353ab798416c0816fc3ef933ed65b7e9934221c31c7ee0c.png] 

**Given:**

Speeds of the four equal segments = 3 km/h, 4 km/h, 7 km/h, and 12 km/h.

Total time taken = 680 minutes = 680/60 hours = 34/3 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Distance = 4 × Distance of one segment

**Calculation:**

Let the equal distance traveled at each speed be d km.

⇒ Total distance = 4d km.

⇒ Total time = (d/3) + (d/4) + (d/7) + (d/12)

⇒ LCM of 3, 4, 7, and 12 is 84.

⇒ Total time = (28d + 21d + 12d + 7d) ÷ 84

⇒ Total time = 68d / 84 = 17d / 21 hours

According to the problem, the total time is 34/3 hours.

⇒ 17d / 21 = 34 / 3

⇒ d = (34 × 21) ÷ (17 × 3)

⇒ d = 2 × 7 = 14 km.

⇒ Total distance = 4d = 4 × 14 = 56 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for n Equal Distances

If an object covers n equal distances at speeds S₁, S₂, ... Sₙ, the average speed is given by the harmonic mean: Average Speed = n ÷ (1/S₁ + 1/S₂ + ... + 1/Sₙ).

General Average Speed Formula

For unequal distances or times, the average speed is strictly the ratio of total distance covered to the total time taken: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).
</p

questions.question: If a+ b + c = 5, a² + b² + c² = 27. and a³ + b³ + c³ = 125 then 4abc =?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct combined identity: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)/2 × [3(a² + b² + c²) − (a + b + c)²]

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 5/2 × [3(27) − 5²]

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 5/2 × [81 − 25] = 5/2 × 56 = 140

⇒ 3abc = 125 − 140 = −15 ⇒ abc = −5

⇒ 4abc = 4 × (−5) = −20

**∴ The correct answer is -20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b + c = 5

a² + b² + c² = 27

a³ + b³ + c³ = 125

**Formula Used:**

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − (ab + bc + ca))

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we find the value of (ab + bc + ca):

⇒ 5² = 27 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 25 = 27 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 25 − 27 = −2

⇒ ab + bc + ca = −1

⇒ Now, substitute all values in the second formula:

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 5 × (27 − (−1))

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 5 × (27 + 1)

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 5 × 28

⇒ 125 − 3abc = 140

⇒ 3abc = 125 − 140

⇒ 3abc = −15

⇒ abc = −5

⇒ We need to find the value of 4abc:

⇒ 4abc = 4 × (−5) = −20

**∴ The correct answer is -20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Alternate Form

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

Square of Trinomial

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
</p

questions.question: Ritika purchased 'x' kg wheat at Rs.30/kg and sold 8 kg of this at Rs. 'x' per kg and remaining at Rs. 45/kg. Overall profit percent earned is 10%, then what quantity of wheat Ritika sold at Rs. 45/kg?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall Selling Price = 30 × 1.10 = Rs. 33/kg.

Equating total SP parts: 8x + 45(x − 8) = 33x

53x − 360 = 33x ⇒ 20x = 360 ⇒ x = 18

Quantity sold at Rs. 45/kg = x − 8 = 18 − 8 = 10 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 30/kg, Overall profit = 10%

Quantity sold at Rs. x/kg = 8 kg

Quantity sold at Rs. 45/kg = (x − 8) kg

**Formula Used:**

Mean SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Alligation ratio = (SP₂ − Mean SP) / (Mean SP − SP₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd1e397aa89bdb403bbae6ee7345ab77a8827f5393cb629151f5ae37df3dfb4c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean Selling Price = 30 × 1.1 = Rs. 33/kg

⇒ Using the Alligation ratio: 8 / (x − 8) = (45 − 33) / (33 − x)

⇒ 8 / (x − 8) = 12 / (33 − x)

⇒ 2 / (x − 8) = 3 / (33 − x)

⇒ 2 × (33 − x) = 3 × (x − 8)

⇒ 66 − 2x = 3x − 24

⇒ 5x = 90

⇒ x = 18

⇒ Quantity sold at Rs. 45/kg = 18 − 8 = 10 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 10 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixtures & Alligation Rule

It allows finding the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price: Quantity 1 / Quantity 2 = (Price 2 − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − Price 1).

Profit and Loss Basics

Selling Price (SP) is calculated as CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100. When multiple parts are sold at different prices, the overall SP is the weighted average of the individual SPs.

Replacement Method

When a quantity 'y' is replaced 'n' times from a total mixture 'x', the remaining quantity of the original substance is given by x × (1 − y/x)ⁿ.
</p

questions.question: L's income is 125 percent of M's income and L's expenditure is 120 percent of M's expenditure. If L's income is 180 percent of M's expenditure, then what is the respective ratio of L's savings and M's savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let M's Expenditure = 100 units.

L's Income = 180% of 100 = 180 units.

L's Expenditure = 120% of 100 = 120 units → L's Savings = 180 − 120 = 60 units.

M's Income = (180 × 100) ÷ 125 = 144 units → M's Savings = 144 − 100 = 44 units.

Ratio of Savings (L : M) = 60 : 44 = 15 : 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

L's Income = 125% of M's Income

L's Expenditure = 120% of M's Expenditure

L's Income = 180% of M's Expenditure

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings ⇒ Savings = Income − Expenditure

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9932d3d88cafaf7fc2f514881b4ed36c7ea3aebc2d7c0104ac4a93d0ed88308.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let M's Expenditure = 100 units

⇒ L's Income = 180% of M's Expenditure = (180 ÷ 100) × 100 = 180 units

⇒ L's Expenditure = 120% of M's Expenditure = (120 ÷ 100) × 100 = 120 units

⇒ L's Income = 125% of M's Income

⇒ M's Income = L's Income × (100 ÷ 125) = 180 × (4 ÷ 5) = 144 units

⇒ L's Savings = L's Income − L's Expenditure = 180 − 120 = 60 units

⇒ M's Savings = M's Income − M's Expenditure = 144 − 100 = 44 units

⇒ Respective ratio of L's savings and M's savings = 60 : 44

⇒ Ratio = 15 : 11

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The fundamental equation is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. If you assume a base value like 100 for one variable, you can easily derive others through basic percentage relations.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions drastically speeds up calculations. For example, 125% = 5/4, 120% = 6/5, and 180% = 9/5.

Ratio Simplification

A ratio remains unchanged when both of its terms are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number. It is always best to express ratios in their simplest fractional form before selecting an option.
</p

questions.question:
The ratio of length to breadth of a rectangular field is 10 : 3. The cost of putting fence around it at Rs. 12 per metre is Rs. 6240.

The area (in m²) of the field is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate = 6240 ÷ 12 = 520 m ⇒ Semi-perimeter = 260 m.

Given L : B = 10 : 3, sum of ratio parts = 13 units.

13 units = 260 m ⇒ 1 unit = 20 m.

Area = 10 units × 3 units = 30 × (20)² = 12000 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 12000 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of length to breadth = 10 : 3

Total cost of fencing = Rs. 6240

Rate of fencing = Rs. 12 per metre

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate per metre

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Area = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35ac557464bbdfa98b31bb2121ea31b6c97f98bb9672ba77232bad52f3e223be.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangular field = 6240 ÷ 12 = 520 m

⇒ Let the length be 10x and breadth be 3x.

⇒ 2 × (10x + 3x) = 520

⇒ 2 × 13x = 520

⇒ 26x = 520

⇒ x = 520 ÷ 26 = 20

⇒ Length = 10 × 20 = 200 m

⇒ Breadth = 3 × 20 = 60 m

⇒ Area of the field = 200 × 60 = 12000 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 12000 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total boundary length of a rectangle. Formula: P = 2 × (L + B), where L is length and B is breadth.

Area of a Rectangle

The 2D space enclosed within the boundary of the rectangle. Formula: Area = L × B.

Fencing Concept

questions.question: A divisor is 15 times the quotient and 3 times the remainder. If the quotient is 12, what is the dividend?

**∴ The correct answer is 2220.**

**__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Dividend = (180 × 12) + 60

Perfect Divisibility

If the remainder is zero, the dividend is perfectly divisible by the divisor, making the divisor and quotient the direct factors of the dividend.

questions.question: The height of a cone is 30 cm. A small cone is cut off at the top by a plane parallel to its base. If its volume is (1)/(27) of the volume of the given cone, then what is the height of the frustum of the cone ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a cone cut by a plane parallel to its base, the volume ratio of the new upper cone to the original cone is the cube of their height ratio: Volume ratio = (Height ratio)³.

Given the volume ratio is 1 : 27, taking the cube root gives the height ratio as 1 : 3.

Height of the small cone = 1/3 of the total height = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm.

Height of the frustum = Total height − Small cone height = 30 − 10 = 20 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total height of the given cone (H) = 30 cm

Volume of the small cone (v) = 1 ÷ 27 × Volume of the given cone (V)

**Formula Used:**

When a cone is cut by a plane parallel to the base, the small cone formed is similar to the original cone.

Ratio of volumes = (Ratio of corresponding heights)³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72e245a0c635b3f184346975dd87b9f7088bbe61d1ee967b0f47165d485565ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of small cone (v) ÷ Volume of given cone (V) = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ (Height of small cone ÷ Total height)³ = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ (h ÷ 30)³ = (1 ÷ 3)³

⇒ h ÷ 30 = 1 ÷ 3

⇒ h = 30 ÷ 3

⇒ h = 10 cm

⇒ Height of the frustum = Total height − Height of the small cone

⇒ Height of the frustum = 30 − 10 = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone with base radius 'r' and height 'h' is given by: V = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h

Volume of a Frustum

For a frustum with height 'h' and base radii 'R' and 'r', the volume is: V = (1 ÷ 3) × π × h × (R² + r² + R × r)

Similarity Property of Cones

When a cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base, the upper section forms a cone similar to the original. The ratio of their volumes is the cube of the ratio of their corresponding heights or radii.
</p
